top_choice_rationale: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) is a chemically new, general method: ligand design turned a substrate-limited bond formation into a routine operation, the catalytic cycle is mechanistically understood, and more than 25 years of independent use in medicinal and process chemistry can be verified. Attribution to two independent laboratories is the cleanest in the slate and the achievement fits in a two-sentence citation. Targeted protein degradation (P001) is a real and consequential second choice, though I find its single citation joins two origins; nitrogenase (P003) has an open mechanism and phase separation (P004) is the least mature in cells, but I still prefer either to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or any credited name in the slate (shared Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr is not related to any proposed laureate)
